data.narrative:
Inertia Enterprises is a Series A nuclear energy company that has raised $450M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a comparables universe of 11 firms across the nuclear energy sector—3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers including Valar Atomics, Helion, and Fuse Energy.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, which uses total capital raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, implies a valuation of $900M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Valar Atomics (Series B, $6.0B), Nano Nuclear Energy (Seed, $808M), and Fuse Energy (Series A, $200M)—produces a median valuation of $808M. The peer range spans $200M to $6.0B, reflecting wide dispersion in nuclear energy valuations at different stages.

Synthesizing both methods yields a triangulated range of $687M (low) to $1.0B (high), with a median of $854M. Key uncertainties include the applicability of the stage-progression multiplier given nuclear energy's capital intensity and variable development timelines, and the substantial peer valuation dispersion ($200M–$6.0B), which limits confidence in the peer-median approach. The analysis supports a valuation band centered near $854M, though execution risk and sector dynamics warrant close reassessment.
